newsitem.title: INDIA: India Shaw Wallace gets merger approval.
newsitem.headline: India Shaw Wallace gets merger approval.

text.p: India approved a proposal to merge the loss-making Doburg Lager Breweries Ltd with liquor major Shaw Wallace and Company Ltd, a Shaw Wallace statement said on Tuesday.
The approval was given by the Board of Industrial Finance and Reconstruction (BIFR), the Indian authority entrusted with reviving loss-making firms.

"The rehabilitation proposal of the Maharashtra-based Doburg Lager Breweries Limited has been approved by the BIFR, paving the way for the sick company's immediate merger with liquor major Shaw Wallace and Company," the statement said.
Ravi Jain, Shaw Wallace managing director, described the merger plan as a shot in the arm for the company's aggressive growth plans in the beer business.
He said: "Shaw Wallace will enhance the Doburg plant capacity by 150 percent taking it to 125,000 hectolitres per annum within the next 60 days". The present capacity is 50,000 hectolitres.
"This will involve a capital outlay of 50 million rupees," he added.

Shaw Wallace said the one-time settlement envisages the repayment of a liability of 194.8 million rupees ($5.44 million) over a period of two years in case of secured loans and four years in the case of unsecured loans.
"Shaw Wallace has already deposited approximately 120 million rupees in a No Lien Account with banks against the one time settlement," it added.

The share swap ratio has been fixed at one Shaw Wallace share for every 60 shares of Doburg. Shaw Wallace will also employ all the Doburg employees without any interruption in their services, the company said.
